CAT.rationale: Caterpillar's Q1 2026 results were undeniably strong: revenue up 22.2% YoY to $17.4B, EPS of $5.47 beating consensus by $0.83, and a record $63B backlog providing multi-year visibility. The Power & Energy segment is a genuine secular growth engine driven by AI data center demand, with Power Generation revenue up 41% YoY. Services revenue reached $24B in 2025, on track toward the $28B 2026 target. However, the stock has already re-rated massively — P/E has expanded from ~17x a year ago to ~44x currently, and P/B from ~9x to ~22x. This is a cyclical industrial trading at a premium typically reserved for high-growth tech. Tariff headwinds of $2.2-2.4B for 2026 are compressing margins (Resource Industries segment profit fell 39% YoY in Q1). The balance sheet shows rising leverage (total liabilities up to $76.9B from $66.9B a year ago, equity flat at ~$18.7B). Operating cash flow was only $1.87B in Q1 vs $3.74B in Q3 2025, and the company deployed $5.7B to shareholders in Q1 alone — a pace that appears to exceed cash generation. While the fundamental trajectory is positive, the valuation has moved far ahead of the fundamentals, leaving limited upside and significant downside risk if the cycle turns or tariff costs persist. The next earnings catalyst (Aug 4, 2026) is too distant to provide a near-term re-rating boost.
